title: Rice Paper Bacon: Layered, Marinated Vegan Bacon Demonstration (Goodful)
summary: This Goodful video presents a vegan bacon technique built around layering two sheets of rice paper, softening them briefly, and cutting them into bacon-strip shapes. The host follows a detailed marinade mixing cream with tamari, nutritional yeast, olive oil, maple syrup, garlic powder, smoked paprika, black pepper, and liquid smoke, then coats both sides of the rice paper pieces. After an oven bake at 400°F (204°C) for about seven to eight minutes, the rice paper bacon achieves a crisp, fatty-like texture. The presenter discusses coating methods, notes the aftertaste of baloney, and highlights ethical considerations about pig farming, eventually rating the result around 8/10 and suggesting the vegan bacon as a strong BLT option. The video credits Edgy Veg as the original recipe source and frames the result as a practical, accessible vegan alternative with environmental and animal welfare implications.

sections.title: Intro and concept
sections.description: The video opens with the host introducing a rice-paper vegan bacon concept and naming Edgy Veg as the original source. The presenter notes rising interest in vegan bacon across platforms like TikTok and Reels, framing the recipe as accessible and aligned with spring rolls and a pantry of rice paper.

sections.title: Rice paper prep
sections.description: Two sheets of rice paper are layered to thicken the bacon, then given a brief water soak to soften. The host uses kitchen scissors to cut the softened sheets into bacon-strip shapes.

sections.title: Marinade preparation
sections.description: The host assembles a marinade consisting of tamari, nutritional yeast, olive oil, maple syrup, garlic powder, smoked paprika, black pepper, and liquid smoke, then mixes it. The discussion includes strategies for coating (dunking vs brushing) and the idea that both sides should be well-coated.

sections.title: Baking and initial results
sections.description: The rice-paper bacon strips are placed in a preheated oven at 400°F (204°C) for about seven to eight minutes. The host notes eyeballing the remaining time, observes the strips turning crispy and fatty-looking, and discusses sensations of crunch versus chew.

sections.title: Observations, ethics, and verdict
sections.description: Post-bake, the host describes the texture as crispy with fatty notes and acknowledges that flavor may not identically replicate pork bacon. The video presents ethical considerations about pigs—citing intelligence and factory farming statistics (97% of pigs in the US). The host argues for reducing pork intake for planetary health and endorses vegan bacon as a strong alternative, suggesting its use on a BLT. The verdict is a favorable 8/10, with encouragement to try and adapt the recipe.
